question.:question/problem:
Consider the matrix $X,$ given by

$$
X=\begin{bmatrix}-9 & -9 & -5 \\ 4 & 1 & -4 \\ 1 & -3 & 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-4{R}_{3}$ on $X?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-4{R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $-4$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =\begin{bmatrix}-9 & -9 & -5 \\ 4 & 1 & -4 \\ 1 & -3 & 1\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-4{R}_{3} \\  & \sim\begin{bmatrix}-9 & -9 & -5 \\ 4+(-4)(1) & 1+(-4)(-3) & -4+(-4)(1) \\ 1 & -3 & 1\end{bmatrix} \\  & \sim\begin{bmatrix}-9 & -9 & -5 \\ 0 & 13 & -8 \\ 1 & -3 & 1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: 3x3 signed integer matrix; first target entry cancels; distinct source/target rows; |k|=2..5
